ゼリーフライ.summary: A local dish from Gyoda. Despite the name, it is not fried jelly. Okara (soy pulp) and potato are mixed with vegetables like carrot and green onion, shaped into ovals, deep-fried without batter and dipped in sauce. One theory says the coin-like shape earned the name zeni-furai (coin fry), which became zeri-furai over time. It has a simple, fluffy flavor and makes a great snack. Try it cheaply at specialist shops in the city, perhaps with a walk around Gyoda's ancient burial mounds.

shops.name: Kanetsukido
shops.query: かねつき堂 行田
shops.comment: A Gyoda favorite for zeri-furai and furai.

shops.name: Komagataya
shops.query: 駒形屋 行田 ゼリーフライ
shops.comment: A Gyoda local restaurant where you can order zeri-furai one at a time.

みそポテト.summary: A local favorite in the Chichibu area: steamed potatoes battered and deep-fried, then topped generously with sweet and savory miso sauce. The fluffy potato, crispy coating and sweet miso make an addictive combination. It was originally eaten as a snack between farm work. You can find it at restaurants, roadside stations and tourist stalls in Chichibu. Enjoy it as a walking snack while visiting Chichibu Shrine or Nagatoro. Locals often make it at home too.

shops.name: Oyasumidokoro Moheji
shops.query: お休み処 もへじ 秩父 みそポテト
shops.comment: Chichibu's only miso potato specialty shop.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Chichibu
shops.query: 道の駅ちちぶ
shops.comment: A roadside station with Chichibu specialties; the shop sells miso potato.

東松山やきとり.summary: A local dish from Higashimatsuyama. Although it is called yakitori, it is not chicken but pork kashira (cheek and temple meat) grilled over charcoal. It is eaten with a spicy miso sauce made with garlic and chili. The nicely marbled pork and spicy miso go perfectly with beer. There are many yakitori shops in the city, and in the evening the savory smell drifts through the streets with the smoke. Each shop's miso sauce is different, so be sure to compare.

shops.name: Yakitori Daimatsuya
shops.query: やきとり 大松屋 東松山
shops.comment: The long-running shop where Higashimatsuyama yakitori began.

shops.name: Yakitori Hibiki Higashimatsuyama
shops.query: やきとりひびき 東松山本店
shops.comment: A popular shop known for miso-sauce yakitori.

秩父わらじかつ丼.summary: A Chichibu specialty: large, thin cutlets as big as straw sandals (waraji), dipped in sweet and savory soy sauce and laid over rice. Two cutlets are common, overflowing the bowl. Because it is not cooked with egg, you can fully enjoy the crispy cutlet and the flavor of the sauce. Many restaurants in Chichibu serve it, each with its own sauce and cutlet thickness. It makes a filling lunch during sightseeing in Chichibu and will leave you full.

shops.name: Yasudaya
shops.query: わらじかつ 安田屋 小鹿野
shops.comment: Founded in the Taisho era; the originator of waraji katsudon.

shops.name: Yasudaya Hinoda
shops.query: 安田屋 日野田店 秩父
shops.comment: A branch near Chichibu Station, easy to visit while sightseeing.

秩父豚みそ丼.summary: A Chichibu specialty of pork marinated in miso, grilled until fragrant and served over rice. Chichibu has a long tradition of preserving meat and vegetables in miso, and this dish is said to have grown out of it. The toasty miso, sweet pork and sauce-soaked rice are irresistible. Each shop uses different miso and cooking methods, and some grill over charcoal. Take your time and enjoy it with views of Chichibu's mountains. A taste you can only find here.

shops.name: Nosaka
shops.query: 豚みそ丼本舗 野さか 秩父
shops.comment: A butamiso-don specialist that often has a line.
shops.access: About 5 min walk from Seibu-Chichibu Station

shops.name: Chichibu Shokudo (Michi no Eki Chichibu)
shops.query: 道の駅ちちぶ 秩父食堂
shops.comment: The roadside station restaurant, with a butamiso-don and soba set.

武蔵野うどん.summary: Udon long eaten in the Musashino area, from western Saitama to the Tama area of Tokyo. The noodles are thick and firm, with a satisfying chew. The classic style is niku-jiru udon: cold noodles dipped in a warm sauce with pork and green onions. In Musashino, once a wheat-growing area, farmers made it for special occasions. Its rustic, hearty flavor is the appeal, and the area has many specialist shops. The more you chew, the more the wheat aroma spreads.

shops.name: Masuya
shops.query: 純手打うどん ますや 東村山
shops.comment: A shop of over 50 years, popular for nikujiru udon boiled over a wood fire.

shops.name: Musashino Udon Takekuni
shops.query: 武蔵野うどん 竹國 所沢
shops.comment: A popular shop near Tokorozawa Station.
shops.access: About 4 min walk from Tokorozawa Station West Exit

深谷煮ぼうとう.summary: A Fukaya home-style dish of wide, flat noodles simmered in soy sauce soup with Fukaya green onions, daikon, carrot and taro. The noodles go in raw, so the soup thickens and warms you to the core. Fukaya is the hometown of Shibusawa Eiichi, called the father of Japanese capitalism, who is said to have loved this dish. It is packed with sweet Fukaya green onions. A warming home-style taste of Fukaya for the cold season, best enjoyed when the onions are in season.

shops.name: Menya Chubee
shops.query: 麺屋忠兵衛 深谷 煮ぼうとう
shops.comment: A nibouto specialty restaurant. Lunch only.

shops.name: Sobagura (Michi no Eki Okabe)
shops.query: 道の駅おかべ そば蔵
shops.comment: Try nibouto at the roadside station restaurant.

浦和うなぎの蒲焼き.summary: Urawa in Saitama City has been famous for grilled eel since the Edo period, using eel caught in local marshes. Eels are no longer caught in the rivers and marshes, but many long-established eel restaurants carry on the tradition. Fragrant grilled eel and rice soaked in sweet and savory sauce make an exceptional combination. Each shop grills and sauces its eel differently, so comparing them is fun. It is close to central Tokyo and easy to visit. Enjoy the plump, tender eel.

shops.name: Masuya
shops.query: うなぎ 満寿家 浦和
shops.comment: A long-established eel restaurant founded in Urawa in the Meiji era.

shops.name: Kojimaya
shops.query: 小島屋 浦和 うなぎ
shops.comment: An eel shop carrying on a 200-year tradition.
shops.access: About 17 min walk from Minami-Urawa Station

川幅うどん.summary: A local dish from Konosu: extremely flat udon more than 5 cm wide. It was created in honor of the Arakawa River, whose width between Konosu and Yoshimi is the widest of any river in Japan. The wide noodles have a unique slippery, chewy texture. Shops serve them in many ways, in hot soup, with cold dipping sauce or with curry. They make a big visual impression, and many people take photos. Stop by when walking along the Arakawa riverbank.

shops.name: Choki-ya
shops.query: 手打うどん 長木屋 鴻巣
shops.comment: A shop over 130 years old, famous for 8 cm-wide kawahaba udon.
shops.access: About 5 min walk from Konosu Station

shops.name: Kuraichi
shops.query: 久良一 鴻巣 川幅うどん
shops.comment: A Konosu udon shop serving kawahaba udon.

草加せんべい.summary: The famous hard, soy sauce-flavored rice crackers of Soka, once a thriving post town on the Nikko Kaido road. Rice is flattened and grilled over charcoal while being brushed with soy sauce. They have a satisfying crunch and a fragrant soy sauce aroma. Legend says they began when a woman at a dumpling shop flattened and grilled her unsold dumplings. There are many cracker shops in the city, and some let you grill your own. Freshly grilled crackers are exceptional.

shops.name: Ikedaya
shops.query: いけだ屋 草加せんべい
shops.comment: Founded in the late Edo period; particular about its soy sauce and rice.

shops.name: Soka Senbei no Niwa (Yamako Senbei)
shops.query: 草加せんべいの庭 山香煎餅本舗
shops.comment: Over 100 kinds of senbei, plus a hands-on grilling experience.

十万石まんじゅう.summary: Saitama's signature manju, made by a confectioner in Gyoda. A moist skin made with mountain yam wraps smooth bean paste. It has an elegant, gentle sweetness and a branded mark on top. Its TV commercial catchphrase, "delicious, too delicious," is well known to Saitama people. The name comes from the rice yield of the Oshi domain once based in Gyoda. You can buy it at shops and stations in the prefecture. It goes well with green tea and is a nostalgic taste for locals.

shops.name: Jumangoku Fukusaya Gyoda Main Store
shops.query: 十万石ふくさや 行田本店
shops.comment: The main store in an old storehouse registered as a cultural property.

shops.name: Jumangoku Kumagaya
shops.query: 十万石 熊谷店
shops.comment: Buy jumangoku manju in Kumagaya.

五家宝.summary: A famous sweet from Kumagaya: puffed glutinous rice bound with starch syrup into sticks and coated in roasted soybean flour (kinako). Enjoy the soft kinako outside and the crisp rice inside. It has a toasty kinako aroma and gentle sweetness and has long been Kumagaya's representative souvenir. It is said to have been made since the Edo period and pairs perfectly with green tea. Available at Japanese sweet shops in Kumagaya. Its simple flavor is its charm.

shops.name: Momijiya Honten
shops.query: 五家宝本舗 紅葉屋本店 熊谷
shops.comment: A gokabo maker founded in the Edo period.

shops.name: Hanatsutsumi
shops.query: 花堤 五家宝 熊谷
shops.comment: A gokabo maker founded in the Meiji era, over 120 years old.

彩果の宝石.summary: Fruit-shaped jelly sweets made by a Saitama confectioner. They come in many flavors and shapes, such as strawberry, melon, peach and grape, and look as beautiful as jewels. The fruit flavor comes through clearly, and you can enjoy the crunchy sugar coating and the soft jelly inside. Their colorful look makes them perfect gifts. Each piece is individually wrapped, so they are easy to share, and assortments are especially popular. Available at shops and department stores in the prefecture.

shops.name: Saika no Hoseki Main Store
shops.query: 彩果の宝石 本店 大間木
shops.comment: The main store, with 19 flavors sold by weight.
shops.access: Omagi, Midori Ward, Saitama (near Higashi-Urawa Station)

shops.name: Saika no Hoseki Factory Store
shops.query: 彩果の宝石 本社 工場直販 さいたま市南区
shops.comment: A direct sales shop attached to the main factory.
